## Summary

The November 14 wrap weighs Burry depreciation concerns, emphasizes real returns on AI spending and reviews CoreWeave execution, Disney legacy drag and Circle expectations. It identifies announced deal volume as a forward indicator for advisory activity.

The depreciation arithmetic is valid under a simple assumption, but dismissing measurement concerns entirely would go too far. Most earnings observations are contemporary diagnoses and several future targets belong to management or consensus. The report does not score personal health disclosures.

<a id="youtube-XkFBPAhK4Os-c002"></a>
### 002. Rising subprime auto delinquencies indicate significant stress in weaker borrowers.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 2:48-3:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkFBPAhK4Os&t=168s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The quoted Fitch series is a selected securitized subprime sample and was not independently inspected here. It should not be relabeled as all auto borrowers.

Assessment test: Compare the original sample, seasonal pattern and broader loan populations.


<a id="youtube-XkFBPAhK4Os-c003"></a>
### 003. Extending a $75 billion asset useful life from three to six years cuts annual straight-line depreciation from $25 billion to $12.5 billion.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 3:23-4:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkFBPAhK4Os&t=203s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The arithmetic is correct for a single fully depreciable cohort with zero residual value and a full year in service. Actual capex includes assets with different lives and start dates.

Conditional reasoning: Annual depreciation is cost divided by useful life: 75/3=25 and 75/6=12.5 billion; pretax accounting earnings differ by 12.5 billion before other effects.

Assessment test: Use asset-level additions, residuals and in-service timing.


<a id="youtube-XkFBPAhK4Os-c004"></a>
### 004. Burry estimates useful-life changes will overstate Meta and Oracle earnings by 21% and 27% by 2028.

**Too early** | Michael Burry, reported by Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 4:33-4:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkFBPAhK4Os&t=273s) | Stance: reported | Horizon: 2028

This is explicitly Burry research, not Eisman own estimate. The 2028 horizon and asset-life assumptions remain unresolved.

Assessment test: Compare economic lives, retirements, impairments and the original model.


<a id="youtube-XkFBPAhK4Os-c005"></a>
### 005. Actual AI returns and cost savings matter more than depreciation choices, so the accounting concern is not central.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 5:03-5:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkFBPAhK4Os&t=303s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Cash economics ultimately matter, but depreciation estimates affect reported margins and can obscure replacement spending or impairments. The issues are related rather than mutually exclusive.

Conditional reasoning: Changing depreciation does not create cash at purchase. Yet future replacement outlays depend on actual useful life, so an incorrect life estimate can also mislead a forecast of sustainable cash returns.

Assessment test: Reconcile cash returns with economic asset replacement and accounting estimates.

## Framework and tools

- Separate accounting timing from actual cash economics.
- Watch construction execution as well as contracted demand.
- Distinguish legacy-business decline from new-business growth.
- Use announced deal volume to assess future advisory activity.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Useful lives and depreciation
- Backlog versus construction schedules
- Segment operating income
- Stablecoin circulation and expense guidance
- Announced versus closed M&A volume
